name: Findstack

sources.title: Get listed page — renders a vendor account signup (professional email + password, or Google)
FAQ — 'I run a software company, how can I get my product listed?' → 'Head across to our Get listed page and submit the product details'
How We Select Software (search-indexed) — 'use this form to submit or claim your software listing'; happy to list tools in a relevant category even if not a 'Best Of' pick

requirements: Software product that fits a B2B software category (directory covers 300+ categories)
Vendor account on findstack.com — signup with professional email (or Google) is the gate before the product submission form
Revenue model is vendor-funded (leads, deals, premium listings) but basic listing is free — 'We include every vendor in our listings, not just those who compensate us'
preparation: Professional email for the vendor account
Product name, URL, category fit, description, pricing details, feature list, integrations
Logo and screenshots for the profile
For a Deal listing instead: contact via /about#contact
workflow: Open https://findstack.com/get-listed and create the vendor account (professional email or Google)
Submit product details via the listing form after signup (or claim the listing if the product already exists in the catalog)
Wait for Findstack review/publication — the listing publishes as a product page plus structured data/Markdown (the catalog is machine-readable via public API and MCP)
Optionally pursue a Deal listing by contacting them separately
watchFor: The /get-listed page looks like a generic signup — it is the vendor gate; the product form comes after account creation
Premium listing upsell exists (enhanced profile media, contact options) — not required for the basic listing
Listings publish as structured data and Markdown readable by AI assistants — copy should be factual, not hype
Premium membership $49/yr mentioned in the FAQ is for BUYERS of deals, not vendors — don't confuse the two
countsAsLive: The product page is publicly reachable at findstack.com/products/<slug> or appears via the public API /api/v1/products search
unknowns: Whether the vendor signup leads directly to a product form or a claim-existing-listing flow first
Link treatment (dofollow/nofollow) on live product pages
